   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  Human Relations Council Liaisons

 FROM:  Christopher Paulson, Human Services Administrator

  Enisha Clark, LCSW, Human Services Outreach Manager

  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services

 DATE:  March 27, 2024

 SUBJECT:  Update to Election Civility Statement

 ATTACHMENTS:  1. City Council Staff Report – Human Relations Commission
  Election Civility Statement for the Community – March 2, 2010
  2. Election Civility Statement (Current)
  3. Election Civility Statement (Final Draft)

INTRODUCTION

At the October 2023 Human Relations Commission meeting, Chair Freeman requested to add to
the November agenda a discussion of updating the Election Civility Statement. The Chair noted
that social media was not a political tool when this statement was created and adopted in 2010
like it is today, and the statement should be updated to reflect that reality.

DISCUSSION

The Human Relations Commission’s (HRC) current civility initiative started in December 2007
when the HRC appointed an ad hoc committee to explore ways to foster civility in our community.
By late 2009, the HRC had begun the process of drafting an election civility statement, starting
with the formation of an ad hoc committee of the Commission. The ad hoc met to draft the
statement before bringing the statement to the full HRC for approval.

From there a Human Relations Commission liaisons meeting was scheduled with the Mayor and
Vice Mayor at the time on November 30, 2009. The HRC Liaisons worked to draft the Election
Civility Statement for the Beverly Hills community which was then approved and adopted by the
full City Council at the March 2, 2010 City Council meeting. The City Council staff report for that
meeting is attached to this report.

The process to update the Election Civility Statement would remain the same as it was in 2010.
At the November 2023 Commission meeting it was agreed for this item to be part of the
Commission’s Civility Ad Hoc which includes Vice Chair Margo and Commissioner Kaiserman.
 Commissioners were also encouraged to return to the December 2023 meeting with ideas and
suggestions for updating the statement. At the December 2023 meeting, then-Chair Freeman
proposed additional language to be added to the existing Election Civility Statement and created
a temporary ad hoc consisting of herself and Vice Chair Margo to work out the details of the
additional language and return to the full Commission with a final draft to review and consider.

The ad hoc of Chair Margo and Commissioner Freeman recommended the draft statement be
presented to the full Commission for review at the January 18, 2024 meeting. The Commission
approved the statement as presented and recommend review and consideration by City Council
Liaisons.

Council Liaisons are requested to review the draft statement with the ad hoc, make any necessary
changes or edits, and then recommend the statement to the full City Council for adoption. If
adopted by the City Council, the statement can be routed to the City Clerk’s office for continued
inclusion in candidate handbooks prior to future municipal elections.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Council Liaisons review the draft statement with the ad hoc, make any
changes or edits, and then recommend the statement to the full City Council for adoption.

   ELECTION CIVILITY STATEMENT
  (Adopted by City Council in 2011)

  The Human Relations Commission of the City of Beverly Hills strives to
  promote positive human relations in all aspects of community life. We
  recognize the significant role of digital media and all online platforms in
shaping public discourse. We encourage all community members to engage
  in online discussion with respect and empathy, fostering an environment
  where diverse perspectives are valued.

  We believe that the examination of diverse candidates and challenging
  issues can be conducted with great civility, without resorting to personal
  attacks or the spread of misinformation..

While our schools may provide civics education in the classroom, we citizens
are obligated to provide our young people with a real-life model of positive
civic behavior that we teach by example. We emphasize the importance of
  honesty and integrity in all aspects of civic engagement. Honesty builds
  trust, and integrity ensures that our community’s values are upheld.
 Together let us exemplify the values of transparency, fairness, and ethical
  conduct to inspire the next generation of civic leaders.

  We hope that every member of this community will join us as we take a
stand in support of an environment where respect and responsible actions
  prevail in all elections and in every aspect of our community life.
   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS

  COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  MEMORANDUM

TO:  Human Relations Council Liaisons

FROM:  Christopher Paulson, Human Services Administrator

  Enisha Clark, LCSW, Human Services Outreach Manager

  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services

  Gregory Barton, Fire Chief

DATE:  March 27, 2024

SUBJECT:  CAGF Process Update

ATTACHMENTS: None

INTRODUCTION

The FY 2024-25 Community Assistance Grant Funding (CAGF) Request for Proposal (RFP)
was released on Thursday, January 18, 2024. The application was available online at
www.beverlyhills.org/cagf, and applications closed on February 29, 2024. A total of 31 complete
applications were received for this application cycle. The sum total of grant requests is
$2,073,499.

This year, staff is recommending a slightly different process, by sorting the organizations into
two groups and removing one of those groups from the CAGF process and entering into a
traditional agreement to pay for services rendered.

DISCUSSION

On March 29, 2024, the HRC CAGF Ad Hoc (Commissioner Kaiserman and Commissioner
Kraushaar) will meet jointly with the Charitable Solicitations Commission (CSC) CAGF Ad Hoc
(Chair Lipton and Commissioner Galen). The Joint Ad Hoc will invite any applicant in for an
interview if either Ad Hoc committee had any questions about the organization’s finances or
programmatic proposal. All new applicants will also be invited for an interview. At this meeting,
the Joint Ad Hoc will produce a set of recommendations to bring to their respective
Commissions.

The HRC Ad Hoc will bring the Joint Ad Hoc’s recommendation to the full Human Relations
Commission at the April 18, 2024 meeting. The Ad Hoc will receive comments from the
Commission and include the HRC-approved recommendations in a joint report to be produced
by the Charitable Solicitations and Human Relations Commissions during their April meetings.
In May, the Ad Hoc representatives from each commission will present the recommendations to

03/27/2024 FY 24/25 Community Assistance Grant Funding
 the City Council Liaisons. In June, staff will present the Council Liaison recommendations to
City Council.

A total of 31 complete applications were received for this application cycle. The sum total of
grant requests is $2,073,499.

However, this year, staff is recommending a slightly different process, by sorting the
organizations into two groups and removing one of those groups from the CAGF process. The
first group of organizations are those that provide crucial services to the community and cannot
be replicated by City-staff. Serious unintended consequences may be experienced by residents
should services not be made available. The City will enter into contractual agreements for
services rendered, based on billable hours for Beverly Hills residents, separately and outside of
the CAGF process.

There are five critical service providers that will be moving towards direct contracts with the city,
based on services rendered for the upcoming fiscal year. These organizations include Jewish
Family Services Los Angeles, Beverly Hills CPR, People Assisting the Homeless (P.A.T.H.),
Step Up on Second, and Bet Tzedek. The anticipated total amount to contract with these five
organizations for Fiscal Year 24/25 is $1,065,000.

The next group of organizations, which are the bulk of grantees, are those that provide a
General Social Service Program that provides quality of life services to the community that are
otherwise not being provided; services are not urgent in nature and no serious consequences
are present should services be delayed. This group also contains a few organizations that
provide Cultural Arts Programs. This is the group that will participate in the CAGF process.

Some additional criteria and metrics that will be requested through the application process and
in the quarterly reporting will be a focus on direct referrals for services from Beverly Hills
residents or Beverly Hills staff, to ensure these grants benefit the Beverly Hills community.

Therefore, the tentative General Fund allocation for CAGF FY 24/25 is $1,112,500. This value is
obtained by starting with the current FY23/24 CAGF budget of $2,177,500 and subtracting the
anticipated amount to directly contract with the five organizations mentioned above, $1,065,00,
leaving $1,112,500 available for CAGF recipients.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Council Liaisons review and support the updates to the CAGF
process, and budget of $1,112,500.

  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, March 27, 2024
  4:30 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  March 27, 2024 / 4:32 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Lester Friedman, Councilmember Lili Bosse, City Manager
  Nancy Coffey, Director of Community Services Stephanie Harris, Fire Chief
  Barton, Human Relations Commission Chair Laura Margo, Human
  Relations Commissioner Noelle Freeman

  1) Public Comment:
  a. Mark Elliot commenting via Zoom: He has concerns over the quality of service
  provided by Bet Tzedek due to both him and several tenants he has talked with
  not receiving a response from Bet Tzedek despite numerous attempts at
  contacting them. He is concerned whether or not the city is getting their money’s
  worth from the contract they are paying Bet Tzedek and if the city keeps track if
  whether or not people referred to them actually get served.

  2) Update to Election Civility Statement:
  a. The goal of these changes is to include the impacts of social media and the internet
  on elections, which was not covered by the original statement. These changes
  particularly focus around spreading online misinformation and personal attacks on
  candidates.
  b. Councilmember Bosse is supportive of the proposed changes as she was
  extremely disappointed at the conduct of people on social media during the last
  election. She is also in favor of looking into consequences for candidates or
  campaign committees that violate the election civility statement.
  c. Vice Mayor Friedman agrees with Councilmember Bosse’s statements, but he is
  concerned about the enforcement of the civility statement in ways other than
  shaming them due to the democratic structures of this country.

  3) CAGF Process Update:
  a. With the adoption of the homelessness plan, city staff is looking to contract with
  organizations that provide critical services that cannot be provided by staff. These
  contracts would be based on services rendered per billed hours outside of existing
  CAGF funding.
  b. Organizations being considered are: Jewish Family Services, Beverly Hills CPR,
  People Assisting the Homeless (PATH), Step Up on Second, and Bet Tzedek.
 Highlights for March 27, 2024
Human Relations Commission Committee

  c. The anticipated total contractual amount between the five organizations for FY
  2024-25 is $1,065,000, which would raise the tentative General Fund funding
  allocated for CAGF in FY 2024-25 to $1,112,500.
  d. 31 applications were received for this funding cycle for CAGF prior to it being
  closed. The first round of review happened in the Human Relations Commission
  Ad Hoc earlier in the day, with the next meeting happening this Friday. During that
  meeting, the 11 first time applicants will be brought in and interviewed.
  e. For the 31 applicants, the total requested funding is $2,073,499. This number does
  not include the 5 contracts from point c.
  f. For the 5 contracts, they will first be based on a projection of how many people
  they expect to use the service. Following the projection, the city will set a cap on
  how many people can use the service in a year and then set a contract rate.
  g. In the event that additional funding is needed for an organization in a year, the
  proposal for additional funding would be brought before the City Council.
  h. Both liaisons view the contract changes for the five organizations as giving the city
  more oversight and control of the provided services as opposed to the traditional
  CAGF structure.
  i. For all the services focusing on the homeless, staff will be analyzing the services
  provided to prevent the city from funding something that they already provide in-
  house due to the programs started over the past 12-18 months.
  j. The five organizations were informed in December about the upcoming changes
  and that they need to submit a different proposal than the standard CAGF
  application.

  4) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: March 27, 2024 / 5:04 PM
